requirements.guidance: Review use case documentation. Pay particular attention to AI features that inform decisions about students (admissions, grades, financial aid eligibility) due to FERPA implications.

requirements.description: Vendor notifies institutional customers at least 30 days in advance before deploying new AI capabilities or materially changing existing AI models that process institutional data.
requirements.guidance: Confirm advance notification procedures for AI changes. Material AI model changes may require institutional re-evaluation of risk.

controls.name: AI Risk Assessment
controls.description: Formal risk assessment process for AI systems prior to deployment.

requirements.description: Vendor conducts formal AI risk assessments before deploying new AI models or significantly updating existing models, evaluating technical, ethical, legal, and societal risks.
requirements.guidance: Request the AI risk assessment methodology. Evaluate whether risk assessments are proportionate to the potential impact of the AI system.

requirements.description: AI risk assessments specifically evaluate privacy risks, including the potential for AI models to reveal sensitive information about individuals or reconstruct training data.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate whether privacy-specific AI risks (model inversion, membership inference attacks) are addressed in risk assessments.

requirements.description: AI risk assessment results are reviewed by senior leadership and appropriate subject matter experts before model deployment, with residual risks formally accepted by an accountable executive.
requirements.guidance: Confirm governance of AI risk acceptance. Risk acceptance for high-impact AI systems should require senior executive sign-off, not just technical team approval.

controls.name: Bias and Fairness Testing
controls.description: Testing AI models for demographic bias and disparate impact.

requirements.description: Vendor tests AI models for demographic bias and disparate impact before deployment and at least annually thereafter, using recognized bias evaluation frameworks.
requirements.guidance: Request bias testing methodology and results summaries. Bias testing should evaluate protected characteristics including race, gender, age, and disability status.

requirements.description: Vendor defines acceptable thresholds for model bias and takes corrective action when testing reveals bias levels that exceed defined thresholds.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate the rigor of bias thresholds and corrective action procedures. Vague commitments to reduce bias without defined metrics are insufficient.

requirements.description: Vendor makes bias testing results available to institutional customers upon request, with sufficient detail to evaluate potential impact on the institution's specific student population.
requirements.guidance: Confirm willingness to share bias testing results. Higher education institutions have particular obligations to avoid disparate impact on student populations.

controls.name: Model Explainability and Transparency
controls.description: Vendor's ability to explain AI model decisions to institutional users.

requirements.description: Vendor provides model cards or equivalent documentation for AI models that make or inform decisions about individuals, describing model purpose, performance metrics, limitations, and known biases.
requirements.guidance: Request model cards for AI features relevant to the institution. Model cards should be sufficiently detailed for technical evaluation.

requirements.description: For AI models that make or significantly inform individual-level decisions, vendor provides human-interpretable explanations of the factors contributing to each decision upon request.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate explanation capabilities for decision-support AI. FERPA and due process considerations may require explainability for student-affecting decisions.

requirements.description: Vendor discloses to institutional users when they are interacting with AI-generated content or AI-assisted responses, rather than human-generated content.
requirements.guidance: Confirm AI disclosure practices. Failure to disclose AI involvement in institutional communications may create legal or reputational risk.

controls.name: AI Training Data Provenance
controls.description: Documentation and governance of data used to train AI models.

requirements.description: Vendor documents the provenance of all training data used for AI models that process institutional data, including data sources, collection methods, and any personal data included.
requirements.guidance: Request training data provenance documentation. Evaluate whether institutional data is used to train AI models and whether this use is disclosed and consented.

requirements.description: Vendor explicitly discloses whether and how institutional data (including student data) is used to train, fine-tune, or improve AI models, and obtains written consent before using institutional data for AI training.
requirements.guidance: Confirm that institutional data is not used for AI training without explicit written consent. Use of student data for AI training may violate FERPA.

requirements.description: Vendor's AI training data governance program addresses data quality, representativeness, and the removal of biased or inappropriate training examples.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate training data governance maturity. Poor training data quality is a root cause of many AI performance and bias issues.

controls.name: Model Security
controls.description: Security controls protecting AI models from adversarial attacks and prompt injection.

requirements.description: Vendor tests AI models for adversarial vulnerabilities including adversarial examples, model evasion, and model inversion attacks, with documented mitigations for identified vulnerabilities.
requirements.guidance: Request adversarial robustness testing documentation. AI models used in security-relevant contexts require specific robustness testing.

requirements.description: For generative AI and LLM-based features, vendor implements prompt injection defenses to prevent malicious user inputs from hijacking model behavior or exfiltrating system prompts.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate prompt injection defenses for any LLM-based features. Prompt injection is a critical vulnerability for LLM applications handling sensitive data.

requirements.description: Vendor monitors AI model behavior in production for anomalies, drift, and potential misuse or adversarial manipulation, with alerting and response procedures.
requirements.guidance: Confirm that AI model monitoring is in place in production. AI models can degrade or be manipulated without human oversight.

controls.name: AI Output Validation
controls.description: Processes to validate the accuracy and appropriateness of AI model outputs.

requirements.description: Vendor implements output validation procedures to detect and filter harmful, inaccurate, or inappropriate AI-generated content before delivery to institutional users.
requirements.guidance: Request output validation methodology. Automated output filtering is particularly important for generative AI features.

requirements.description: Vendor maintains performance benchmarks for AI model accuracy, precision, recall, and other relevant metrics, with automated alerts when production metrics fall below thresholds.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate whether performance monitoring is in place. Degraded AI model performance can have direct impact on institutional users and decisions.

requirements.description: Vendor provides institutions with the ability to report inaccurate or inappropriate AI outputs, with a defined review and correction process.
requirements.guidance: Confirm reporting and feedback mechanisms. User feedback loops help improve model quality and catch systemic issues.

controls.name: Human Oversight Requirements
controls.description: Human review and oversight requirements for AI-assisted decisions.

requirements.description: For AI features that inform decisions about individuals (students, employees), vendor's product design requires meaningful human review before any decision is finalized.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate whether human oversight is technically enforced or merely recommended. Fully automated decisions about individuals may create legal obligations under GDPR Art. 22 or FERPA.

requirements.description: Vendor provides institutional administrators with controls to configure the level of human oversight required for AI-assisted decisions, including the ability to disable fully automated decisions.
requirements.guidance: Confirm institution-configurable oversight settings. Institutions should be able to enforce human review requirements that match their own policies and legal obligations.

requirements.description: Vendor trains institutional users on the limitations of AI outputs and the importance of critical human review, and provides guidance on appropriate reliance on AI-generated recommendations.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate vendor training materials on AI limitations. Users who over-rely on AI recommendations without understanding limitations may make poor decisions.

controls.name: AI Ethics Policy
controls.description: Vendor's formal commitments to ethical AI development and deployment.

requirements.description: Vendor maintains a publicly accessible AI ethics policy describing their commitments to fairness, accountability, transparency, privacy, and avoidance of harmful uses of AI.
requirements.guidance: Review the AI ethics policy for specificity and enforceability. Generic ethics statements without specific commitments or accountability mechanisms provide limited assurance.

requirements.description: Vendor has an internal AI ethics review process, including review by diverse stakeholders, for AI features that could have significant impact on individuals or communities.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate the internal AI ethics review process. Diversity of perspectives in ethics review is associated with better identification of potential harms.

requirements.description: Vendor has published use cases for which AI will not be used, and enforces these restrictions through product controls and employee training.
requirements.guidance: Review the AI use restrictions list. Vendors with well-defined prohibited use cases demonstrate thoughtful AI governance.

controls.name: Generative AI Policy
controls.description: Governance of large language model (LLM) and generative AI features.

requirements.description: Vendor discloses which generative AI or LLM models (including third-party models such as GPT-4, Claude, Gemini) are used in the product, including whether institutional data is sent to third-party AI providers.
requirements.guidance: Confirm disclosure of all AI model providers. Data sent to third-party LLM APIs represents a subprocessor relationship requiring DPA coverage.

requirements.description: Vendor implements controls to prevent institutional data input into generative AI features from being used to train third-party foundation models, and obtains written confirmation from LLM providers.
requirements.guidance: Request the LLM provider data use commitments. Most commercial LLM APIs have options to opt out of training data use; confirm vendor has exercised these options.

requirements.description: Vendor implements output review and content safety filtering for generative AI features, including controls to prevent generation of harmful, discriminatory, or factually incorrect content.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate content safety measures for generative AI features. Outputs that violate content policies or contain hallucinations can create institutional liability.

controls.name: AI Incident Response
controls.description: Procedures for detecting, reporting, and remediating AI-specific incidents.

requirements.description: Vendor has defined AI-specific incident types (model failure, bias incident, AI misuse, adversarial attack, data poisoning) and has documented response procedures for each.
requirements.guidance: Request the AI incident response procedures. AI incidents require different response procedures than traditional security incidents.

requirements.description: Vendor notifies affected institutions within 48 hours of discovering an AI incident that has produced materially incorrect outputs, caused harm to individuals, or exposed sensitive data.
requirements.guidance: Confirm AI incident notification commitments. AI incidents affecting student-facing decisions require prompt notification.

requirements.description: Vendor maintains a log of AI incidents, including near-misses, and conducts post-incident reviews to identify systemic issues and improve model governance.
requirements.guidance: Request AI incident tracking metrics. Organizations that track near-misses demonstrate proactive AI risk management.

controls.name: AI Vendor and Third-Party Assessment
controls.description: Assessment of AI components and models sourced from third parties.

requirements.description: Vendor assesses the security, privacy, and ethical practices of all third-party AI model providers before integration, including evaluation of the provider's AI governance program.
requirements.guidance: Request the AI vendor assessment methodology. Third-party AI models introduce risks that differ from traditional software dependencies.

requirements.description: Vendor's agreements with third-party AI providers include data protection, confidentiality, and usage restriction provisions at least as protective as those in the vendor's institutional customer contracts.
requirements.guidance: Request confirmation that AI provider agreements include equivalent data protection obligations. Flow-down requirements are critical for AI subprocessors.

requirements.description: Vendor reassesses third-party AI providers at least annually and has a process to transition away from AI providers that fail to meet required security or privacy standards.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate AI vendor lifecycle management. Vendors without a process to exit problematic AI providers cannot effectively manage AI supply chain risk.

categories.name: Privacy
categories.description: Comprehensive privacy program controls covering privacy by design, consent management, data subject rights, sensitive data handling, cross-border transfers, and privacy incident response. HECVAT v4 introduces 69 new privacy questions across these controls.

controls.name: Privacy by Design
controls.description: Integration of privacy principles into product and service design.

requirements.description: Vendor's product development process formally incorporates Privacy by Design (PbD) principles, including data minimization, purpose limitation, and privacy as the default setting.
requirements.guidance: Request documentation of how PbD is implemented in the SDLC. Evaluate whether privacy engineers or privacy champions are embedded in development teams.

requirements.description: Privacy requirements are defined as acceptance criteria in user stories and product specifications, with privacy-related defects tracked through the standard issue management process.
requirements.guidance: Ask for examples of privacy requirements in product specifications. Privacy as an afterthought is a leading cause of privacy incidents.

requirements.description: New product features that involve collecting, processing, or sharing personal data require privacy review and sign-off before release.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate the privacy review process for new features. Privacy sign-off should be a release gate, not an optional step.

controls.name: Privacy Impact Assessments
controls.description: Formal privacy impact assessments for new processing activities.

requirements.description: Vendor conducts Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) for all new or materially changed data processing activities, using a documented methodology aligned with NIST Privacy Framework or ISO/IEC 29134.
requirements.guidance: Request PIA templates and examples. Evaluate whether PIAs are proportionate to the risk and cover all relevant privacy harms.

requirements.description: For processing activities that are likely to result in high risk to data subjects (large-scale processing, special category data, automated decision-making), vendor conducts a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) meeting GDPR Article 35 requirements.
requirements.guidance: Confirm DPIA procedures for high-risk processing. DPIAs are a legal requirement under GDPR for certain processing activities.

requirements.description: PIA/DPIA results are reviewed by the Privacy Officer and relevant stakeholders, with findings tracked and remediated before processing begins.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate the PIA/DPIA governance process. Assessments completed but not acted upon provide no privacy benefit.

controls.name: Lawful Basis for Processing
controls.description: Documentation of legal basis for each processing activity.

requirements.description: Vendor maintains a Record of Processing Activities (RoPA) documenting the lawful basis for each personal data processing activity, as required by GDPR Article 30.
requirements.guidance: Request a RoPA summary or confirm its existence. The RoPA should be specific enough to identify the lawful basis for each type of institutional data processed.

requirements.description: For processing institutional data, vendor relies on contractual necessity or legitimate interest as the primary lawful basis, and does not rely on consent for processing that institutions cannot meaningfully withhold.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate the appropriateness of lawful basis claims. Consent is not an appropriate lawful basis for most vendor data processing of student data.

requirements.description: Vendor provides a mapping of processing activities to lawful bases upon request, enabling institutions to verify GDPR compliance obligations.
requirements.guidance: Request the lawful basis mapping. This documentation enables institutions to assess their own GDPR compliance when using vendor services.

controls.name: Consent Management
controls.description: Platform and procedures for managing end-user consent.

requirements.description: Vendor provides a consent management platform or capability that allows institutions to configure, collect, record, and manage end-user consent for processing activities that require it.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate consent management tooling. Confirm that consent is collected in a GDPR-compliant manner (freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous).

requirements.description: Vendor records consent with a timestamp, version of the privacy notice consented to, and the mechanism by which consent was given, and retains these records for at least three years.
requirements.guidance: Request consent record retention policies. Consent records must be auditable and retained for the duration of any regulatory inquiry.

requirements.description: Vendor supports consent withdrawal at any time without penalty to the user, and implements withdrawal within 72 hours by ceasing the consented-to processing.
requirements.guidance: Test consent withdrawal procedures. Consent that cannot be meaningfully withdrawn is not valid under GDPR.

controls.name: Cookie and Tracking Compliance
controls.description: Compliance with cookie consent and tracking regulations.

requirements.description: Vendor's product implements a cookie consent management platform that presents users with granular consent options by cookie category (necessary, functional, analytics, marketing) before setting non-essential cookies.
requirements.guidance: Test cookie consent implementation. Confirm that non-essential cookies are not set before consent is obtained, including on first page load.

requirements.description: Vendor maintains a current cookie inventory documenting all cookies set by the product, their purpose, duration, and whether they involve third-party data sharing.
requirements.guidance: Request the cookie inventory. Undisclosed third-party tracking cookies are a common compliance gap.

requirements.description: Vendor complies with the IAB TCF or equivalent industry standard for programmatic advertising consent where the product serves advertising, and does not serve behavioral advertising to known minors.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate whether advertising-related tracking is applicable. For student-facing products, behavioral advertising without appropriate consent is a FERPA and COPPA risk.

controls.name: Children's Data Protection
controls.description: Protections for data of minors including compliance with COPPA and FERPA.

requirements.description: Vendor has implemented specific controls for products used by or with individuals under 18, including under-13 controls required by COPPA and protections for student records under FERPA.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate the vendor's COPPA and FERPA compliance posture. Products used in K-12 or with student populations require specific technical and policy controls.

requirements.description: Vendor does not serve behavioral advertising to users of K-12 or student-facing products, and does not build behavioral profiles on minors for commercial purposes.
requirements.guidance: Confirm behavioral advertising restrictions for minors. Commercial use of student data is prohibited under FERPA and many state student privacy laws.

requirements.description: Vendor has signed or is willing to sign a Student Data Privacy Consortium (SDPC) Data Privacy Agreement or equivalent state-specific student data privacy agreement.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate readiness to sign state student data privacy agreements. Many states require signed agreements before vendors can process student data.

controls.name: Sensitive Data Categories
controls.description: Handling of special categories of sensitive personal data.

requirements.description: Vendor identifies and applies enhanced protections to special categories of personal data including health/medical data, biometric data, financial account data, race/ethnicity, religious beliefs, and sexual orientation.
requirements.guidance: Request the sensitive data handling policy. Confirm that enhanced protections include encryption, access restriction, audit logging, and DPIA requirements.

requirements.description: Vendor collects biometric data only with explicit consent and in compliance with applicable biometric privacy laws (e.g., Illinois BIPA, Texas CUBI, Washington My Health MY Data Act).
requirements.guidance: Evaluate biometric data collection practices and legal compliance. Biometric privacy law violations carry significant statutory damages.

requirements.description: Vendor does not collect or process health data covered by HIPAA without executing a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) and does not combine FERPA-protected student data with health data without appropriate authorization.
requirements.guidance: Confirm BAA requirements and execution for HIPAA-covered data. The intersection of FERPA and HIPAA in higher education requires careful analysis.

controls.name: Right to Access, Erasure, and Portability
controls.description: Technical and operational support for data subject rights requests.

requirements.description: Vendor provides a documented process for institutions to fulfill data subject access requests (DSAR) on behalf of their users, including a machine-readable export of all personal data within 30 days.
requirements.guidance: Test DSAR fulfillment capabilities. Evaluate whether fulfillment requires manual effort or is supported by self-service tooling.

requirements.description: Vendor supports right-to-erasure requests by providing a verified deletion process that removes personal data from all production systems, backups, and archives within a defined and disclosed timeframe.
requirements.guidance: Confirm erasure scope and timeframes. Erasure from backups typically takes longer than production systems; ensure this is disclosed.

requirements.description: Vendor supports data portability by exporting all personal data associated with an individual in a structured, machine-readable format (JSON, CSV, XML) upon authenticated request.
requirements.guidance: Request documentation of portability export formats. Confirm that exported data is complete and includes all data types held by the vendor.

controls.name: Automated Decision-Making
controls.description: Controls for automated decisions that significantly affect individuals.

requirements.description: Vendor identifies all automated decision-making processes in its products that produce legal or similarly significant effects on individuals, and discloses these to institutions.
requirements.guidance: Request a list of automated decision-making processes. GDPR Article 22 and analogous state laws restrict fully automated decisions affecting individuals.

requirements.description: For automated decision-making covered by GDPR Article 22 or equivalent laws, vendor provides data subjects with the right to request human review of the decision, contest the decision, and obtain an explanation.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate human review mechanisms. Confirm that these rights are technically supported and not merely aspirational policy commitments.

requirements.description: Vendor regularly audits automated decision-making processes for disparate impact on protected groups and provides audit results to institutions upon request.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate the frequency and rigor of disparate impact audits for automated decisions. Higher education institutions have particular obligations under Title VI and Title IX.

controls.name: Marketing Consent
controls.description: Controls governing use of institutional data for marketing purposes.

requirements.description: Vendor does not use institutional user data for direct marketing, cross-selling, or retargeting without explicit opt-in consent from the institution and each individual user.
requirements.guidance: Review the contract and privacy policy for marketing use restrictions. Use of student data for vendor marketing is generally prohibited under FERPA.

requirements.description: Vendor provides institutions with controls to disable all marketing communications to institutional users through the vendor's product, separate from security and operational notices.
requirements.guidance: Confirm that marketing opt-out is configurable at the institutional level. Institutions should be able to completely block vendor marketing to students.

requirements.description: Vendor maintains email marketing lists in compliance with CAN-SPAM, CASL, and GDPR email marketing requirements, including suppression list management.
requirements.guidance: Request marketing compliance documentation. Confirm that unsubscribe requests are honored promptly and consistently across all marketing systems.

controls.name: Data Sharing Agreements
controls.description: Agreements governing sharing of institutional data with third parties.

requirements.description: Vendor does not share institutional data with third parties outside the scope of contracted services without explicit written authorization from the institution.
requirements.guidance: Confirm the non-disclosure and restricted sharing provisions in the DPA. Request a list of all third parties with whom institutional data is currently shared.

requirements.description: For any authorized sharing of institutional data with third parties, vendor executes data sharing agreements that require the recipient to maintain equivalent privacy and security protections.
requirements.guidance: Review data sharing agreement templates. Flow-down protections should be at least as strong as those in the institutional customer contract.

requirements.description: Vendor maintains an audit trail of all instances of institutional data shared with third parties and provides this log to institutions upon request.
requirements.guidance: Request data sharing audit log capabilities. Institutions need visibility into who has received their data to comply with FERPA disclosure requirements.

controls.name: Privacy Training
controls.description: Privacy training for vendor staff handling institutional data.

requirements.description: All vendor employees and contractors with access to institutional personal data complete annual privacy training covering applicable laws (FERPA, GDPR, CCPA), data handling requirements, and incident reporting.
requirements.guidance: Request training curriculum and completion metrics. Evaluate whether training is specific to the types of data handled or generic corporate compliance training.

requirements.description: Vendor provides role-specific privacy training to engineers, product managers, and customer-facing staff, covering relevant privacy requirements for their specific function.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate role-specific training depth. Engineers need training on PbD and secure coding; customer success staff need training on data handling and DSAR procedures.

requirements.description: Vendor tracks privacy training completion and enforces mandatory completion as a condition of maintaining access to systems processing institutional data.
requirements.guidance: Confirm enforcement of training completion. Training that is optional or not enforced has limited effect on privacy culture.

controls.name: Cross-Border Transfer Mechanisms
controls.description: Legal mechanisms for cross-border transfers of personal data.

requirements.description: For transfers of EU personal data to countries without EU adequacy decisions, vendor relies on current Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) incorporating the EU-approved 2021 modules, with a completed Annex I describing the specific transfer.
requirements.guidance: Request executed SCCs and completed Annexes. Confirm that SCCs use the 2021 version and cover all transfer scenarios (controller-to-processor, processor-to-processor).

requirements.description: Vendor has executed or will execute the EU-US Data Privacy Framework certification, UK International Data Transfer Agreement (IDTA), or equivalent mechanism for transfers to US-based processors.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate transfer mechanism options. The EU-US DPF provides a streamlined transfer mechanism for certified vendors. Verify current certification status.

requirements.description: Vendor provides a Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) for any transfer to a country where surveillance laws could undermine the protections of SCCs, assessing the risk and describing supplementary measures.
requirements.guidance: Request TIAs for non-adequate country transfers. TIAs should be recent (within 12 months) and reflect current legal landscape.

controls.name: Privacy Incident Response
controls.description: Specific procedures for responding to privacy incidents and regulatory complaints.

requirements.description: Vendor maintains a privacy incident response plan separate from or integrated into the security incident response plan, with specific procedures for privacy breaches, regulatory complaints, and data subject rights disputes.
requirements.guidance: Request the privacy incident response procedures. Privacy incidents (e.g., wrongful disclosure, consent violations) require different handling than security incidents.

requirements.description: Vendor notifies affected institutions within 48 hours of discovering a privacy incident involving institutional personal data, including details of the nature of the incident, categories of data affected, and remediation steps.
requirements.guidance: Confirm privacy incident notification commitments. Some privacy incidents trigger regulatory notification obligations with tight deadlines.

requirements.description: Vendor cooperates with institutional responses to regulatory inquiries and data subject complaints, including providing evidence of compliance and corrective action plans within requested timeframes.
requirements.guidance: Confirm cooperation obligations for regulatory inquiries. Institutions may face regulatory action if vendors fail to support timely responses.

controls.name: Privacy Program Metrics
controls.description: Measurement and reporting on privacy program performance.

requirements.description: Vendor tracks and can report privacy program performance metrics including DSAR volume and response times, privacy incident frequency, training completion rates, and PIA completion rates.
requirements.guidance: Request privacy metrics summaries. Quantitative metrics demonstrate privacy program operational maturity beyond policy documentation.

requirements.description: Privacy program metrics are reviewed by the Privacy Officer and executive leadership at least quarterly, with trends and gaps reported to the board or equivalent governance body annually.
requirements.guidance: Evaluate governance oversight of privacy metrics. Board-level privacy reporting indicates executive accountability for privacy program performance.

requirements.description: Vendor benchmarks its privacy program against industry standards (NIST Privacy Framework, ISO/IEC 29100, or equivalent) and can describe its current maturity level and improvement roadmap.
requirements.guidance: Request privacy program maturity assessment or self-evaluation. Vendors that benchmark against established frameworks are more likely to have systematic privacy programs.
